chapterTitle: The Minimal Dossier for a Discovery
instructions: Analyze this chapter segment faithfully. Capture its thesis, role, ideas, representative evidence, objections, and qualifications. Cite source unit IDs.

units.text: The Minimal Dossier for a Discovery

Write exactly what you claim and the domain in which you claim it. Separate “we have an example,” “it works on this set,” “there is a proof,” and “it generalizes.” Do not use the word “revolutionary” as a substitute for any of them.

Keep the closest papers or solutions, not only those against which the proposal looks strong. Record which comparisons you have not yet managed to make. An incomplete literature search can support “I did not find it,” not “nobody has done it.”

What observation would count against it? What result would support the simpler alternative? If no imaginable observation could count, explain whether the proposal is philosophical, interpretive, or not yet sufficiently operationalized, instead of presenting it as an experimental result.

Preserve the inputs, definitions, method version, environment, evaluation criteria, and relevant outputs. Separate examples used in development from those used in final evaluation. Protect data that cannot legitimately be published and specify what an independent evaluator can check.

Use proportionate formulations: supported under the conditions tested; refuted in this form; inconclusive; unverified. Record costs and limitations, not just success. Do not ask the model for a certificate of importance; ask it to help you prepare for the encounter with evidence.
